items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.
Mayor McCabe offered personal reflections on her own learning journey, in particular that she is reading The Knowing by Tanya Talaga.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

Mayor McCabe also reflected on the end of Black History Month and the work that The Caribbean Canadian Association of Waterloo Region, Congress of Black Women of Canada Waterloo Chapter, and other organizations have put into organizing events all month long. She noted the Mount Zion Lutheran Church held an event celebrating Black History on February 23. It was their 20th Anniversary of hosting Black History Month events.

items.title: Property Acquisition – 250 Lincoln Road
notes: Philippe Elsworthy, Resident of Waterloo spoke in favour of the acquisition and for more affordable housing, but against the demolition of the St. Columba Church due to its architectural and historical significance. He asked Council for a Cultural Heritage Evaluation on the Church.
Kae Elgie, Resident of Waterloo asked Council to consider a community centre in place of the Church, in order to decentralize community centres and make them more accessible to residents.
Justin McFadden, Joel Cotter and Astero Kalogeropoulos responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Consideration of Notice of Motion Given at Previous Meeting
notes: Mayor Dorothy McCabe – US Proposed Tariff Response

Craig Sloss, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the need to expand the scope of the motion to explore the use of other social media platforms and include restricting the use of U.S. social media platforms, especially those controlled by U.S. government officials and those whose moderation policies are inconsistent with the Ontario Human Rights Code. Cari Van Niekerk responded to questions of Council. Craig Sloss also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Freeman wanted to thank IPPW and Parks staff for their work on snow removal over the last few weeks. She had a question regarding the height of some of the snow piles in the City, and how we could bring them down as people are having trouble seeing around them. She also asked about the clearance of snow on catch basins, as things are starting to melt and water is building up and then freezing. Lastly, she asked who is responsible for snow removal at fire hydrants.

Bob Henderson responded that getting rid of snow banks and snow loading are other exercises for snow plow drivers when they’re not in the plow. There is a priority list with snow banks that are causing sightline issues, the LRT, school zones, regional roads and more. Regarding catch basins, he has been in talks with Leigh McDermott about going through the City and looking for spots where they can avoid flooding. Regarding fire hydrants, they have been requesting help from residents to help clear them. While it is not the responsibility of residents, it is very helpful when they do. Fire Services staff are also working to help clear them.

Cari Van Niekerk also responded that they are trying to get messages out publicly asking residents to help out. There was great coverage last week about Fire Services crews digging out hydrants, but there are 2600 of them across the City so it’s a big process. Catch basin messaging is queued up to run this week to ask residents for some assistance there.

Leigh McDermott also mentioned that the storm crews are now on a high priority list of response for the catch basins and grates across the City. Today, they were coordinating with Fire Services with what they’re doing with the hydrants and what City Utilities is doing. There are three different divisions – Transportation, City Utilities, and Fire Services – all working together on this.

Mayor McCabe had a question regarding old newspaper and real estate boxes throughout the community. She was wondering if these something the City is able to remove and if there is a process to cut the chains. Bob Henderson responded that there is a process and they try to contact the owners first to remove them.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Roe wanted to highlight that the Canadian Clay and Glass Gallery annual tea party fundraiser is back this year. She attended the February 23 event with Councillor Freeman. There are two other dates coming up: March 16 and May 11. It’s a lovely event and helps raise money for a National Gallery here in Waterloo.

Councillor Wright wanted to highlight that the Coldest Night of the Year Walk was Saturday, February 22, and they raised 106% of goal. It shows how much attention the community is paying to the homelessness crisis that we are facing. She wanted to encourage people to continue supporting SHOW and other housing providers.
Mayor McCabe wanted to remind people of provincial election coming up on Thursday, February 27.

motions.item_title: Consideration of Notice of Motion Given at Previous Meeting
motions.text: WHEREAS contrary to terms of the existing United States Mexico Canada Agreement as well as to the long standing strong and productive economic and political relationship between Canada and the United States, the US President threatened to impose 25% tariffs on Canadian goods as of February 1st and although he has subsequently delayed the tariffs by thirty days they remain a real threat; and WHEREAS tariffs could lead to a halt of the supply chain and create economic uncertainty in municipalities of all sizes; and WHEREAS municipalities are the foundation on which the Canadian economy is built, and as such municipalities should offer our support towards a united and strong Team Canada response; and WHEREAS municipalities have significant purchasing power through our capital and infrastructure programs, with the City of Waterloo’s capital program for 2025 being $200 million alone, while the Association of Municipalities of Ontario cite that infrastructure spending across Ontario in the next 10 years is expected to exceed $250 billion; and WHEREAS Federal and Provincial leaders are encouraging all Canadians to Buy Canadian; and WHEREAS City of Waterloo and the broader region is proud and honoured to be home to numerous U.S. based international students, academic professionals, and institutional thought leaders, along with prominent USA companies whose presence has greatly contributed to our quality of life, economic development, innovation, and employment opportunities; and WHEREAS longstanding partnerships highlight the strong, mutually beneficial economic ties between Canada and the United States, fostering collaboration in technology, manufacturing, and research sectors. Maintaining these free-trade practices will promote continued strong growth and shared prosperity on both sides of the border; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT THE CITY OF WATERLOO: Stands with Team Canada on the message that tariffs are not in the best interests of Canadian or American residents, organizations, businesses and employees; AND calls on the Federal and Provincial governments to work with municipalities on measures to protect Canadians and businesses; AND calls on the Waterloo Economic Development Corporation (WEDC), through the Business Economic Support Team Waterloo Region (BEST WR), to develop an action plan to support Waterloo Region businesses and our collective economic interests; AND calls on the Federal and Provincial governments to better enable municipalities to explore procurement opportunities that exist within other trade agreements such as the Comprehensive Economic Trade Agreement; AND calls on the Federal and Provincial government to work collaboratively and urgently to remove trade barriers between provinces and territories, understanding that language requirements should continue to be respected for Quebec; AND calls on City of Waterloo staff to explore options for limiting the impact of the potential United States’ sanctioned tariffs on City Services and review current procurement processes for opportunities to increase purchases from Canadian sources; AND further that a copy of this motion be forwarded to the Right Honourable Justin Trudeau, Prime Minister of Canada, The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, local and area MP’s, MPP’s and Heads of Council, The Association of Municipalities of Ontario and the Federation of Canadian Municipalities.
